problem: A persisted faster-GPU comparison omitted the built-in CPU runtime used as its baseline. Replacing only that CPU executable left the old certificate eligible for automatic GPU selection.

observed_red.result: The unchanged measured comparison worked; after only the isolated CPU executable changed, selected_with incorrectly still returned a GPU launch spec.

changes: Certificate schema 2 / configuration schema 3 binds the actual built-in CPU executable and bounded build-info content receipts, in addition to the existing GPU, model, hardware, selectors and inference configuration.

Status selection uses current receipts only. A cold CPU receipt keeps the saved certificate and reports runtime_verification_required without hashing files. Actual launch admission refreshes only for Automatic Windows/Linux with an eligible saved certificate; unchanged receipts are reused.

Missing, oversized or changed CPU baseline files invalidate optional GPU qualification and request another explicit test. This does not increment GPU failure counters or launch an automatic benchmark/download. Normal CPU admission remains available and performs its own integrity checks.
Calibration retains and rechecks the original CPU receipts through both trials. Replacement during driver capture or calibration cannot be hidden by a newly refreshed receipt.
The settings component labels a pending runtime check neutrally, without claiming active acceleration or displaying a failed test.

validation.browser: Existing acceleration-ui.mjs passed in headless installed Chrome with fictional Windows/Linux component fixtures; includes the new pending status. No native GPU inference.
validation.independent_review: Core and frontend read-only reviews found no remaining P1/P2 in this scope. Directory relocation conservatively requires retesting; hashing is cancellation-checked before/after, not per chunk; loader-wide atomic dependency identity is not claimed.

limits: No model request, real GPU benchmark, model download, native installer or optional component build in this change. Synthetic selection fixtures are not proof of device performance, memory or energy improvement.
The actual launch-prewarm integration test is Windows/Linux-only and was not executed by the local macOS run; same-head platform CI must confirm it.

Linux driver provenance remains session-scoped. The baseline identity includes its directory; relocation conservatively requires a new test. This change does not add arbitrary external shared-library dependency tracking.
Per-task calibration and complete GPU/device coverage remain open. CUDA/Vulkan remain independently downloaded components; explicit CPU and Apple Metal preferences are unchanged.

Q16 complex mixed-language minutes and Q9 real-audio name recall remain open. The original 68-case quality gate is unchanged; no repeated stopped prompt/newline experiment was run. Version 0.3.5 is not released.
